customer.name: Customer
customer.description: Someone hungry, ordering from the Plum app or the website.

restaurant.name: Restaurant
restaurant.description: The kitchen staff who accept an order and mark it ready.

courier.name: Courier
courier.description: Rides or drives the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.

support.name: Support agent
support.description: Answers customers and couriers when something goes wrong.

ordering.name: Ordering
ordering.description:
Everything a customer touches: browsing menus, building a basket, paying.

The **Order API** is the only way in. It keeps orders in Postgres and announces every new
order on the **Order events** bus, which is how **Delivery** hears about it.

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.description:
Finds a courier for each order and follows it to the door.

Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking keeps the customer's map moving.

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: Push, SMS and email, from one place, so no other system talks to a messaging provider.

backoffice.name: Back office
backoffice.description: Tools for Plum's own staff. Nothing here is visible to customers or couriers.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.description:
Takes card payments and sends refunds. Plum never sees a card number.

[Provider status](https://status.stripe.com)

mapbox.name: Mapbox
mapbox.description: Maps, address lookup and travel times.

customer-app.name: Customer app
customer-app.description:
The app on the customer's phone. Browse, order, pay and watch the courier arrive.

Keeps nothing but the basket and the session.

web.name: Website
web.description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are rendered on the server so search engines see them.

kitchen-tablet.name: Kitchen tablet
kitchen-tablet.description: Rings when an order arrives. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** when it can be collected.

order-api.name: Order API
order-api.description:
Every client talks to this, and nothing else talks to the **Orders DB**.

- `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
- `POST /orders` places an order
- `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one

orders-db.name: Orders DB
orders-db.description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.

data.name: orders
data.note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds; the order stays.

columns.name: total
columns.note: Stored in cents because rounding broke the first tax run.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.note: Copied from the menu at order time. Menus change; receipts must not.

menu-cache.name: Menu cache
menu-cache.description: Menus, kept for five minutes. A restaurant's edit shows up on its own once the entry expires.

data.name: Keys
data.limits: Oldest unused go first at 256 MB
data.note: A restaurant's edit takes up to five minutes to show up. Shorter put too much load on Postgres.

events.name: Order events
events.description:
One message for every change to an order: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

Dispatch reads from it, and so does the warehouse.

data.name: order-events
data.note: Keyed by order id, so one order's messages stay in order.

menu.name: Menu
menu.description: Serves a restaurant's menu from the cache, and from the database when the cache is cold.

basket.name: Basket
basket.description: Holds what the customer picked and asks **Pricing** for the running total.

pricing.name: Pricing
pricing.description:
Works out the total: items, delivery fee (by distance) and any promotion.

The delivery fee uses the travel distance from Mapbox, rounded up to the next 500 m.

snippets.title: Delivery fee

checkout.name: Checkout
checkout.description:
Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

Nothing is charged until the restaurant accepts. A rejected order releases the hold.

status.name: Order status
status.description: Moves an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, and announces each step.

snippets.title: Accepting an order
snippets.text:
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'

refunds.name: Refunds
refunds.description: Returns money to the card, then marks the order refunded. Support can refund in full or by line.

courier-app.name: Courier app
courier-app.description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Sends the courier's position every five seconds while a job is open.

dispatch.name: Dispatch
dispatch.description:
Turns each new order into a courier on the way.

It reads `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.

tracking.name: Live tracking
tracking.description: Passes the courier's position to the customer's map. A position older than a minute is dropped.

fleet-db.name: Fleet DB
fleet-db.description: Couriers, their vehicles, and their last known position.

matcher.name: Matcher
matcher.description: Ranks the idle couriers near a restaurant by how soon each could be there.

eta.name: ETA
eta.description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and the courier's vehicle.

offers.name: Offers
offers.description:
Offers a job to one courier at a time and waits 30 seconds for an answer.

A refusal or a timeout moves on to the next courier.

notifier.name: Notifier
notifier.description: Picks push, SMS or email for each message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.

templates.name: Message templates
templates.description: The wording of every message, per language.

admin.name: Admin dashboard
admin.description: Restaurants, delivery zones, promotions and the weekly reports.

support-console.name: Support console
support-console.description: Look up an order, see where the courier is, issue a refund.

warehouse.name: Data warehouse
warehouse.description: Every order event, kept for reporting. Nothing reads it except the **Admin dashboard**.

  customer:

    name: Customer
    description: Someone hungry, ordering from the Plum app or the website.
  restaurant:
    type: actor
    name: Restaurant
    description: The kitchen staff who accept an order and mark it ready.
  courier:
    type: actor
    name: Courier
    description: Rides or drives the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.
  support:
    type: actor
    name: Support agent
    description: Answers customers and couriers when something goes wrong.
  ordering:
    type: system
    name: Ordering
    description: |
      Everything a customer touches: browsing menus, building a basket, paying.

      The **Order API** is the only way in. It keeps orders in Postgres and announces every new
      order on the **Order events** bus, which is how **Delivery** hears about it.
  delivery:
    type: system
    name: Delivery
    description: |
      Finds a courier for each order and follows it to the door.

      Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking keeps the customer's map moving.
  notifications:
    type: system
    name: Notifications
    description: Push, SMS and email, from one place, so no other system talks to a messaging provider.
  backoffice:
    type: system
    name: Back office
    description: Tools for Plum's own staff. Nothing here is visible to customers or couriers.
  stripe:
    type: system
    name: Stripe
    external: true
    description: |
      Takes card payments and sends refunds. Plum never sees a card number.

      [Provider status](https://status.stripe.com)
  twilio:
    type: system
    name: Twilio
    external: true
    description: Sends the SMS messages.
  mapbox:
    type: system
    name: Mapbox
    external: true
    description: Maps, address lookup and travel times.
  customer-app:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Customer app
    tech: React Native
    code:
      - apps/customer/
    description: |
      The app on the customer's phone. Browse, order, pay and watch the courier arrive.

      Keeps nothing but the basket and the session.
  web:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Website
    tech: Next.js
    description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are rendered on the server so search engines see them.
  kitchen-tablet:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Kitchen tablet
    tech: Android
    description: Rings when an order arrives. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** when it can be collected.
  order-api:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Order API
    tech: Node, Fastify
    code:
      - services/order-api/
    description: |
      Every client talks to this, and nothing else talks to the **Orders DB**.

      - `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
      - `POST /orders` places an order
      - `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one
  orders-db:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Orders DB
    tech: Postgres
    description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.
    data:
      - name: orders
        kind: table
        limits: Kept 7 years, then archived
        note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds; the order stays.
        columns:
          - {name: id, key: primary}
          - {name: customer_id, to: customers}
          - {name: total, note: Stored in cents because rounding broke the first tax run.}
        rows:
          - [o_1042, c_77, 2490]
          - [o_1043, c_12, 1380]
          - [o_1044, c_77, 990]
      - name: order_items
        columns:
          - {name: order_id, key: primary, to: orders}
          - {name: item_id, key: primary}
          - quantity
          - {name: unit_price, note: Copied from the menu at order time. Menus change; receipts must not.}
        rows:
          - [o_1042, i_31, 2, 1245]
          - [o_1043, i_8, 1, 1380]
      - name: refunds
        limits: Kept with its order
        columns:
          - {name: id, key: primary}
          - {name: order_id, to: orders}
          - amount
          - reason
        rows:
          - [r_9, o_1044, 990, Wrong item]
      - name: baskets
        limits: Swept after 24 hours
        columns:
          - {name: id, key: primary}
          - {name: customer_id, to: customers}
          - items
          - expires_at
  menu-cache:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Menu cache
    tech: Redis
    description: Menus, kept for five minutes. A restaurant's edit shows up on its own once the entry expires.
    data:
      - name: Keys
        limits: Oldest unused go first at 256 MB
        note: A restaurant's edit takes up to five minutes to show up. Shorter put too much load on Postgres.
        columns: [Key, Value, Expires]
        rows:
          - ["menu:{restaurantId}", "{ items, prices, hours }", 5 min]
          - [menu:r_42, '{ "items": 31 }', 3 min left]
  events:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Order events
    shape: queue
    tech: Kafka
    description: |
      One message for every change to an order: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

      Dispatch reads from it, and so does the warehouse.
    data:
      - name: order-events
        kind: topic
        limits: Kept 7 days, 6 partitions
        note: Keyed by order id, so one order's messages stay in order.
        columns: [Key, Value]
        rows:
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "placed", "total": 2490 }']
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "accepted" }']
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "picked-up" }']
  menu:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Menu
    description: Serves a restaurant's menu from the cache, and from the database when the cache is cold.
  basket:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Basket
    description: Holds what the customer picked and asks **Pricing** for the running total.
  pricing:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Pricing
    code:
      - services/order-api/src/pricing.ts
    description: |
      Works out the total: items, delivery fee (by distance) and any promotion.

      The delivery fee uses the travel distance from Mapbox, rounded up to the next 500 m.
    snippets:
      - title: Delivery fee
        language: typescript
        text: |-
          // Mapbox answers in metres. Round up to the next 500 m.
          const km = Math.ceil(meters / 500) / 2
          const fee = Math.max(MIN_FEE, BASE_FEE + km * PER_KM)
  checkout:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Checkout
    code:
      - services/order-api/src/checkout.ts
    description: |
      Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

      Nothing is charged until the restaurant accepts. A rejected order releases the hold.
  status:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Order status
    description: Moves an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, and announces each step.
    snippets:
      - title: Accepting an order
        text: |-
          UPDATE orders
          SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
          WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'
  refunds:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Refunds
    description: Returns money to the card, then marks the order refunded. Support can refund in full or by line.
  courier-app:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Courier app
    tech: Kotlin, Swift
    description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Sends the courier's position every five seconds while a job is open.
  dispatch:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Dispatch
    tech: Go
    code:
      - services/dispatch/
    description: |
      Turns each new order into a courier on the way.

      It reads `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.
  tracking:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Live tracking
    tech: Go, WebSocket
    description: Passes the courier's position to the customer's map. A position older than a minute is dropped.
  fleet-db:
    type: store
    in: delivery
    name: Fleet DB
    tech: Postgres, PostGIS
    description: Couriers, their vehicles, and their last known position.
  matcher:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: Matcher
    code:
      - services/dispatch/matcher.go
    description: Ranks the idle couriers near a restaurant by how soon each could be there.
  eta:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: ETA
    description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and the courier's vehicle.
  offers:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: Offers
    description: |
      Offers a job to one courier at a time and waits 30 seconds for an answer.

      A refusal or a timeout moves on to the next courier.
  notifier:
    type: app
    in: notifications
    name: Notifier
    tech: Node
    description: Picks push, SMS or email for each message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.
  templates:
    type: store
    in: notifications
    name: Message templates
    tech: Postgres
    description: The wording of every message, per language.
  admin:
    type: app
    in: backoffice
    name: Admin dashboard
    tech: React
    description: Restaurants, delivery zones, promotions and the weekly reports.
  support-console:

  warehouse:
    type: store
    in: backoffice
    name: Data warehouse
    tech: ClickHouse
    description: Every order event, kept for reporting. Nothing reads it except the **Admin dashboard**.

steps.name: Step animations
steps.description:
One pair of shapes for each way a step can travel, named for the animation they play.

Each animation has a flow of its own with a single step to click through: Send, Call, Event, Callback, Flash, Bolt drop,
Send with a word, Fail, Timeout, Lost, Rejected, Intercepted (twice: by a shape and by a name), Duplicated, Delayed and Share
(Flash has two, because the step before sets it off).

**Every step animation** plays them all: press **P** to watch them one after the other.

structure.name: Flow structure
structure.description:
One set of shapes for each way steps can be grouped: **Repeat**, **Branch**, **Parallel** and **Flow link**.

Each has a flow of the same name, with the chip, lane tabs and progress bar that go with it.

performance.name: Performance
performance.description:
One shape for each thing a load test can show, named for what it shows.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every load effect**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.

states.name: Shape states
states.description:
One shape that goes through every state, and one that holds another shape in a state.

Play **Every state** to watch a shape start, run, degrade, stop, restart and run again, and **State inside a shape** to see a shape show that something inside it is not running.

time.name: Runs over time
time.description:
A run measured over time instead of over load, with events on its timeline that set the state of a shape.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every state over time**, then press **Play**, drag the slider or click an event.

send-from.name: Send · from
send-from.description: `animation: send`. Something runs one way along the line. The sender does not wait.

send-to.name: Send · to
send-to.description: Takes the envelope in with a squash.

effects-from.name: Effects · from
effects-from.description: `animation: { kind: send, effect: bounce }`. What the moving label does on its way, besides travelling. None of them bends its shape.

effects-to.name: Effects · to
effects-to.description: Sits down the slope from its sender, so the label runs along a slanted line and shows it stays level.

call-from.name: Call · from
call-from.description: `animation: call`. The envelope goes, the sender waits, and the reply comes back.

call-to.name: Call · to
call-to.description: Takes the envelope in, then answers.

event-from.name: Event · from
event-from.description: `animation: event`. A bolt runs along the line, and the receiver flashes.

callback-from.name: Callback · from
callback-from.description: `animation: callback`. A ring leaves this shape and a bell runs to the subscriber.

callback-to.name: Callback · to
callback-to.description: The subscriber. A ring goes out when the bell arrives.

after-source.name: Flash · source

source.name: Source

dots-few.name: Few calls

dots-many.name: Ten times the calls

dots-slow.name: Same calls, slower

calls-lost.name: Lost calls

b-in.name: Source B
